$comment: Hand-authored feature reality manifest. Every feature the public docs claim is listed here exactly once. `status` is what the code does today; `tests` is the authoritative list of test ids that prove it (empty means unproven, and no docs page may render the feature as available). A test id is `path#exact test name`, and check-docs.ts fails if the file is absent. A test in `tests` proves the docs agree with the source unless the row carries a `coverage` note saying otherwise; proving the source behaves as documented is what `plannedTestIds` tracks. A row with `manualCheck` cannot be settled by CI at all and names the sign-off that did. Validated by scripts/check-docs.ts (checkFeatureManifest) and by the gate suites under aartiq-browser/tests/. The human-readable companion is aartiq-browser/docs-audit/feature-triage.md.

baseline.note: Rows are derived by reading source, and the four gate suites (Genmoji, shortcuts, deep links, platform integration) re-derive their facts from source on every run, so they cannot go stale silently. Verified against 0c2da24d: all 94 gate tests pass against main's code and npm run docs:check is clean apart from three standing warnings. One row's evidence had genuinely moved and was corrected - http-api.native-bridge cites a single bridgeApp.use middleware calling checkLocalRequest with requireToken: true (main.js:1259-1272), because there are zero per-route call sites; the claim itself always held. Line-number pointers were re-pinned against main. The Linux duplicate-registration finding and both bridge tables are asserted by tests/docs-platform-integration-match-source.test.js, which passes against main unchanged.

statusValues.works: A real entry point exists and behaves as documented. Still requires a passing test before docs may call it available.
statusValues.partial: Something real happens, but not what the docs say, or only on one platform, or only the UI half exists.
statusValues.missing: No entry point, or the documented entry point is never wired to anything.
statusValues.unsafe-by-design: The documented behaviour would let an external origin act without approval. Do not implement as documented; remove the parameter/claim and gate it.

decisionValues.implement: Keep the documented feature and make the code match it, behind a failing test.
decisionValues.remove-from-docs: The claim cannot be made safely or truthfully. Delete it from the docs page; do not build it.
decisionValues.maintainer-decides: Blocked on a maintainer decision. Do not implement and do not delete until answered.

features.title: Local HTTP bridge on 46203 (native panels + CLI + agent API)
evidence: aartiq-browser/main.js:1245 startNativeMacUiBridge()
aartiq-browser/main.js:1259-1272 bridgeApp.use middleware calls checkLocalRequest with requireToken: true, so it runs for every route on the listener rather than per route
aartiq-browser/src/lib/local-server-auth.js checkLocalRequest / extractToken / isHostAllowed / isOriginAllowed
aartiq-browser/src/lib/agent-api/server.ts:74 resolveAgent, :82 callTool
aartiq-browser/src/lib/agent-api/server.ts:98 the agent API authenticates each request the same way
features.notes: The one real local HTTP surface, and it is already token-gated and loopback-bound. This is the section the port-3000 docs should be rewritten from. Note resolveAgent auto-registers unknown agents with config.defaultTrust. The manifest previously pointed at docs/mcp-settings:239, a page that no longer exists; until the Apple page was rewritten, nothing on the live site documented this bridge by port. Re-read 2026-10-04 against 8033d541 after docs:check reported that two cited evidence files had changed. The token gate still holds, but it moved: it used to be per-route calls to checkLocalRequest(requireToken: true) and is now a single bridgeApp.use middleware (main.js:1297) that covers every route on the listener. extractToken now also accepts X-Aartiq-Native-Token, which is the header scripts/aartiq-cli.js and the Swift panels already send; without it every CLI and native-panel request would 401.
features.coverage: Verified by reading against 8033d541 and by the existing tests/local-server-auth.test.js, which exercises checkLocalRequest directly. No test asserts that the middleware is actually mounted on the listener, so a future refactor could drop the app.use and the suite would stay green. tests/local-bridge-auth.test.js#every-route-requires-the-token is still owed.

features.notes: page_find reads a tab that is already open and issues no network request, so it is the cheaper path whenever the answer is on screen. It exists because a search is real egress: it sends the user's query to a third party and returns a different page. Refs bind by a data-aartiq-ax stamp the collector writes onto actionable nodes only — blanket stamping perturbed page code that queries the DOM — with backendNodeId as first-priority identity.

features.notes: Two tools rather than one tool with a submit flag, because filling a form is reversible and submitting one is not. fill_form carries the input verb and never submits; form_submit is sideEffecting and passes the verb gate. Three bugs were found by these tests and fixed: typeScript emitted a bare clearFirst identifier (ReferenceError on every type_ref), contenteditable detection relied only on el.isContentEditable so a plain div reported as filled, and fillFormScript fell back to document.forms[0] and could land a fill in an arbitrary form or submit one.
features.coverage: Form filling is covered at the script level, including the framework-setter path, checkbox and select semantics, and the submit rules. No test drives form_submit through the registry's verb gate with a rejected approval, so the end-to-end refusal path is argued from registry.ts:43-57 rather than exercised.

features.notes: Risk is low because it reads pages the user asked it to read. The claim is the unit of verification rather than the article, which is what keeps '450 million dollars' and '450 million euros' from being matched into false agreement. Domains are re-derived from each claim's own URL instead of trusted from the caller, so subdomains cannot fake independence. A last source is named only when publication timestamps are reliable; otherwise the answer is unknown with the reason attached, because without the reason a caller retries and guesses anyway. Reported as partial in the UI when a contradiction is unresolved rather than when it is resolved.
features.coverage: Claim extraction, verification, last-source selection, budget clamping and the full IPC path are covered. Deliberate limit, stated rather than hidden: extractClaims surfaces only numeric claims with a named subject, so disputed qualitative findings never reach the contradictions panel. That is a false negative rather than a false positive, and it means the coverage percentage reflects numeric agreement specifically, not overall source agreement. A test asserting that a disputed non-numeric claim is surfaced would fail today, so this limit is load-bearing documentation rather than an oversight.
